# =============================================================================
# FULL ACCEPTANCE RUN — end to end, every path the program has, one pass
# =============================================================================
#
#   How to run it:  Tools -> Advanced -> Run acceptance test...  (the app does
#                   the rest: session folder, sleep lock, the run, one file)
#   Where it lives: INSIDE the app, since v0.6.32 — there is nothing to download.
#                   Source: src/platterpus/rig_scripts/fullacceptance.txt
#   What it costs:  it depends on the RUN SIZE you pick when it starts:
#                     Quick     about 15 minutes  (does it still work?)
#                     Standard  about an hour     (is a normal rip right?)
#                     Full      4 to 6 hours      (LEAVE IT RUNNING OVERNIGHT)
#                               measured: 4h14m (2026-09-22, 247 steps) and
#                               5h33m (2026-09-26, 320 steps, the sum of its
#                               report's step times), both on the Pioneer rig;
#                               the script is 431 steps now. The run
#                               states its own estimate when it starts
#                               and again after section E (run-estimate)
#                   Full rips the whole disc TWICE (once fast, once with every
#                   track read at least three times) plus seven short partial
#                   rips.
#                   ONLY FULL counts toward a version or a handshake close.
#
# RUN SIZES are cut from THIS ONE FILE. Each section's first line is
# `run-size <size>`, naming the SMALLEST run that includes it, so Quick is
# inside Standard is inside Full by construction and no section inherits its
# size from the one before (docs/testing.md §5.bj). A smaller run records every
# section it leaves out as declined, so its transcript still lists them.
#
# NOTHING IN THIS FILE NEEDS EDITING. No album name, no track count, no path,
# and — as of this version — no cyanrip build tag either. Put any ordinary
# audio CD in the drive, start it, and go to bed.
#
# AND IT IS RE-RUNNABLE, which it was not before. Every `album` line carries
# `(run)`, expanding to this run's own timestamp, so a second run never lands on
# the first run's folders. Before that, a re-run raised "Album already ripped"
# on every rip; the file answers that prompt in exactly ONE place (§H, on
# purpose), so the other seven rips were refused behind an unanswered modal and
# the 2026-08-25 attempt lost sixteen of its seventeen failures — and all of T1 —
# to it. **You no longer need to move the previous run's output aside.**
#
# §F and §H still name the SAME album deliberately: §H exists to raise that
# prompt and answer it with `click=new`, and `(run)` is stable within one run so
# that collision still happens exactly where it is wanted.
#
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# BEFORE YOU START — two things, and only two
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Be on the newest Platterpus. Tools -> Setup & Updates... -> Check for updates, or download the
#    AppImage from the releases page.
# 2. Be on the cyanrip build THIS Platterpus expects — which is **not** always
#    the newest one, and **not** always the one that installs without a warning.
#    Tools -> Setup & Updates... -> Check for cyanrip updates, and TAKE WHATEVER OFFER IT MAKES:
#    a plain one-click install if that is what appears, and the warned
#    "Install it anyway" if that is what appears instead. Either way, accept it.
#
#    Read that twice if you remember the old wording, because it said the
#    opposite. Until v0.6.36 this comment told you to take the offer ONLY if it
#    was a plain one-click install, and to refuse a warned one. That is right
#    BETWEEN handshake rounds and exactly wrong WHILE ONE IS OPEN — and a round
#    being open is the only time anybody re-reads this. Section A asserts the
#    build UNDER REVIEW, and a build under review is by definition one no closed
#    round has approved, so its offer is the warned one. Refusing it is what
#    ends the night at section A, four seconds in, having spent no drive time
#    and produced no evidence. It has now done that twice.
#
#    Yes, the warned build makes every rip report `unapproved`. That is the
#    record being honest about an open round, not a fault, and it is precisely
#    what the run exists to produce evidence for.
#
#    Do not reach for a channel toggle to decide this, and do not look for a
#    BUILD TAG in this comment: THIS FILE NAMES NO BUILD, on purpose. Which one
#    is wanted changes every time a handshake round opens or closes, and this
#    file ships inside a release — so anything written here freezes on the day
#    it was built and cannot learn that the answer moved. Both previous attempts
#    were wrong within days, and each one sent operators to a build section A
#    refuses. The app holds that fact in one place and checks it — which is why
#    step 2 above is the whole answer, and there is no second copy of it here.
#
#    The rule ABOVE was the same failure one level up: not a frozen build tag,
#    but a frozen answer to "which offer is the right one", which moves for the
#    same reason and just as often. "Take whichever one it offers" is the form
#    that cannot go stale, because it delegates to the surface that knows.
#
#    IF THE CHECK OFFERS YOU NOTHING SECTION A ACCEPTS, THERE IS A SECOND
#    ROUTE, AND YOU WILL NEED IT WHILE A ROUND IS OPEN ON AN UNPUBLISHED BUILD.
#    The in-app check reads the fork's RELEASE MANIFEST, so it can only offer
#    builds the fork has published. A handshake round may open on a commit they
#    have nominated but never released — round 16 did — and then the dialog's
#    best honest answer is "your build is current", which is true of the
#    manifest and is not the build section A wants. Taking it ends the night at
#    section A.
#
#        Tools -> Setup & Updates... -> Choose a build...
#
#    It lists every build THIS version can install, each with a marker and a
#    reason: `✓ approved` is what a closed round verified, `⚠ under-review` is
#    the build an open round is examining, `⚠ test-pin` is one both projects
#    nominated for a joint hardware session. **The build this run needs is
#    already selected when the dialog opens** — it is derived from the same
#    constant section A checks, so the two cannot disagree. Click Install.
#
#    THIS FILE STILL NAMES NO BUILD, for the reason three paragraphs up, and
#    that is exactly why the route is a MENU ITEM rather than a commit: the list
#    and the pre-selection are generated from that constant, so neither can be
#    the stale half of a pair. A `⚠` here is the record being honest about an
#    open round, not a warning to heed — every rip will report `unapproved`,
#    which is the evidence the run exists to produce.
#
#    (There is a terminal equivalent, `--install-ripper list` and
#    `--install-ripper <commit>`, and it is the same function behind the same
#    step engine. It is the older route: this paragraph used to send you there
#    and admit in a parenthetical that the menu had no GUI caller. It has one as
#    of 0.6.45 — an excuse written into operator instructions is still a manual
#    step, and the whole point of this program is not to hand one back.)
#
#    Section A asserts the exact expected build and STOPS THE RUN in the first
#    few seconds if you are not on it — before any drive time is spent.
#
#    That stop is real as of this version. It used to be a promise this file
#    could not keep: nothing but `abort` ends a batch and this file never used
#    it, so a wrong ripper produced a FAIL on line ~20 and then six hours of
#    evidence about the wrong binary. The cyanrip fork read the old sentence and
#    relayed it to the operator (round 14 lap 11 §J7). `abort-if-failed` below is
#    what makes it true.
#
# Everything else is in this file.
#
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# WHY THE ORDER IS WHAT IT IS
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Maintainer directive: *"fresh start, rip, every test there is, all of them.
# this needs to be a good pass fail test"* — the gate on 0.7.100. And KDD-35: a
# version number is a claim about the field, not about CI. Every defect that
# mattered in August was found on hardware with the suite green throughout.
#
# LEAST-LIKELY-TO-FAIL FIRST, deliberately, and it has a cost. Sections A-E are
# near-certain passes that take about five minutes; the first rip is section F.
# Putting the cheap checks first means a broken build or a wrong ripper is
# caught before hours of drive time, and the transcript reads as a widening
# cone — identity, then settings, then validation, then UI, then disc, then
# audio, then the derived formats, then the long one.
#
# The cost: if section F fails, A-E having passed tells you almost nothing about
# why. Accepted. The alternative spends the night before learning the ripper was
# not installed.
#
# THE RULE THAT MAKES THIS SAFE TO LEAVE UNATTENDED: a FINDING never stops the
# batch. Only `abort-if-failed` does, at three preconditions (A the wrong ripper,
# B an unknown offset, E the disc not identified). Every other check fails loudly
# and the run continues. A run that stops at the first problem hides every
# problem behind it, and a disc pass costs hours you do not get back.
#
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# WHAT THIS RUN IS FOR: the hardware close of whichever handshake round is open
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# *One hardware acceptance pass on the RELEASED pair* — the cyanrip build the open
# round is reviewing, against the current Platterpus release. The §T list below
# began as round 14's close condition CC-2 (its lap 1); the sections still cover it.
#
# Round 13's CC-2 measured a mid-round TEST PIN, so satisfying it would have
# closed a round on evidence about a build nobody installs. This tests what ships.
#
#   §T1  a `-Z` rip that GENUINELY re-reads, and keep the log     -> section N
#   §T2  `-T unicode` end to end on a title carrying `<` and `:`  -> sections F, H
#   §T3  `-x -I`, the probe-only cache invocation                 -> section P
#   §T4  an interrupted rip, on hardware                          -> section I
#   §T5  an Enhanced CD, if one turns up                          -> not scripted
#
# T5 is deliberately absent: it needs a disc we may not own, the fork says it is
# not a blocker, and "no such disc available" is a different claim from "none".
#
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# WHAT THIS RUN CANNOT ASSERT — read the transcript and the bundle for these
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Stated up front rather than buried, because a verdict implying more than it
# checked is worse than a shorter one.
#
#   * THAT THE AUDIO IS BIT-PERFECT. `wait-for-rip` waits for the worker to
#     disappear; it does not grade the rip. The AccurateRip verdict is in the
#     report and the log, CTDB's only in the report; `rig-check` judges neither.
#     The bundle carries both files. Read them.
#   * WHETHER DIALOG TEXT IS CLIPPED. A rendering fact at your font size and DPI
#     that no assertion can see. Section D takes screenshots; a person must look.
#   * OVERREAD (`-O`). It has run on the BDR-209D and it HUNG THE DRIVE ~23
#     minutes. Never enabled here; section Q asserts it is still off.
#   * `-f` READ-OFFSET AUTODETECTION. Never run on this rig.
#   * C2 ERROR REPORTING. This drive reports it unsupported, so a green run is
#     not evidence about C2.
#   * DAMAGED MEDIA, and therefore paranoia's actual error correction.
#   * A NON-ZERO `Read stalls:` COUNT. A silent watchdog is not a working
#     watchdog; healthy media cannot produce the other branch.
#   * THE WELL-FORMED ENHANCED CD branch. Exercised by nothing, anywhere.
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

log =============================================================
log FULL ACCEPTANCE RUN - end to end, one pass
log order: cheapest and least likely to fail first
log the first rip is section F; the long one is section N
log =============================================================

# THE BASELINE: every user setting, SET to its shipped default or KEPT on purpose.
# Before this, the run borrowed whatever you had: thirteen of your settings rode
# along into every rip, including the read speed and "Move finished rips to",
# which change what a rip does. Your own settings come back when the session ends
# (the app restores them, on every exit). `tests/test_rig_scripts.py` fails if a
# user setting is missing from this block, so a setting added tomorrow has to be
# decided here rather than inherited from the operator. Every size runs this.
set rip_goal fast_verified
set track_template %A/%d/%t - %n
set disc_template %A/%d/%d
set track_template_unknown Unknown Artist/Unknown Album/%t - Track %t
set disc_template_unknown Unknown Artist/Unknown Album/Unknown Album
set auto_launch_picard off
set auto_eject_after_rip off
set notify_on_completion on
set cover_art embed
set save_additional_art on
set max_retries 5
set force_overread off
set secure_rerip_matches 2
set secure_rerip_dynamic on
set rerip_offset_variant on
set read_speed_mode auto_ladder
set read_speed 0
set ctdb_verify_after_rip on
set verify_flac_after_rip on
set recompress_flac_after_rip off
set write_eac_log_after_rip off
set output_format flac
set mp3_vbr_quality 0
set update_channel stable
set ripper_channel stable
# The session points this at its own rips folder, inside the session folder.
keep output_dir
# The session turns this off, so no test album is moved into your library.
keep library_dir
# `set-drive-offset` in section B owns these two: the drive's offset, not a typed one.
keep read_offset
keep override_read_offset
# This machine's own tool path, not a test value.
keep metaflac_path
# The run's own machinery: the script that is running, and how it was started.
keep test_script_path
keep test_script_autorun

# Debug logging ON for the whole run: the one baseline value that is not the
# shipped default, on purpose. A defect found at 4am is only as diagnosable as
# the log, and this is the one setting that changes how much of the run is
# recoverable afterwards. Restored in section Q.
set debug_logging on
expect debug_logging on
snapshot atstart

# --- A. IDENTITY: which binary is about to be graded -----------------------
# FIRST, always. Every claim below is about a specific build, and a result that
# looks wrong must be attributable rather than guessed at. A build tag we do not
# recognise reads as "not determined", never as a pass.
#
# This also arms the `(ripper)` placeholder used by the album titles further
# down: it expands to the installed build tag, read from the banner captured
# here. If this step is removed, those `album` steps FAIL and say so rather than
# writing the literal text — an unexpanded placeholder would give two rips the
# same folder while looking like it worked.
#
# `expect-ripper-under-review` TAKES NO ARGUMENT, and that is the fix for a
# defect that recurred three times in two days. This file used to name an exact
# build tag; the fork then published two more betas on the channel our own
# installer resolves, so an operator who followed our instructions installed the
# build we sent them to and was told here that it was wrong. The verb now reads
# the constant the handshake record derives, so a pin move fails in CI instead
# of at 2am on your rig.

# AND THE PAIR MUST BE THE NEWEST ONE. Round 30's D3, agreed with the fork and
# ruled by our operator (O1, option A): a run tests only the newest pair. The
# step above proves the installed ripper is the build this app reviews; it
# cannot see that the fork has since released a newer build, or that we have
# released a newer app, and a run on either stale pair passes it and then spends
# a night producing evidence about a pair nobody will ship (the fork's round 30
# lap 3 S4). `expect-newest-pair` reads both projects' releases NOW, the fork's
# manifest across both channels (a new build goes to beta until its run passes,
# O3) and ours on the beta channel, where every `v0.*` tag of ours is.
#
# A pair it CANNOT show is newest fails too, and that is deliberate: the reads
# need the network, and so does every MusicBrainz and AccurateRip step after
# this, so a run that could not make them would not be evidence either.
log --- A. identity: which ripper is installed ---
run-size quick
cyanrip --version
expect-exit 0
expect-cyanrip platterpus-fork
expect-ripper-under-review
expect-newest-pair
snapshot identity

# A4, TASKS "Cold-container start: two container entries at launch". The first
# container command of a launch now runs alone (container_gate.FIRST_ENTRY), and
# a probe that had to wait for it logs a line saying so. Whether it did is in
# this launch's own log, from before this script started; `app-log` copies the
# lines into the transcript (info, never a failure). No line means no probe
# waited: the container was warm, or one command ran at a time.
log A4 (TASKS "Cold-container start"): did a probe at launch wait for the first container command, and did one run anyway after the wait?
app-log for the first container command

# WHICH LINK IN THE RIPPER CHAIN FAILS TO EXIT — gathered, never asserted.
#
# Two consecutive rig mornings (2026-08-26, 2026-08-27) produced ZERO rips and
# neither failed at ripping: both ended mid-probe with `cyanrip --version`
# printing its banner in full and then not returning, until a 60s timeout killed
# it. The cyanrip fork showed three independent ways the hang is not cyanrip and
# asked for three shell commands to be run by hand. This is those commands.
#
# It records `info` and moves on. A wrapper that hangs from an interactive shell
# does not affect this run — the app pipes its I/O — so failing here would abort
# a six-hour pass over something that changes no rip.
probe-ripper-wrapper

# THE FIRST OF THREE PLACES THIS FILE MAY STOP, and the distinction is the point.
#
# The rule above — "a failing step does NOT stop the batch" — is about FINDINGS,
# and it is right: a run that halts on the first problem hides every problem
# behind it. It is the wrong rule for a PRECONDITION. A wrong ripper does not
# make the next six hours partially useful; it makes them evidence about a
# different subject, which is exactly what the handshake exists to prevent
# (two artifacts from the same ripper under different app versions are not
# interchangeable evidence).
#
# So: preconditions abort, findings do not. The other two: B's offset, E's disc.
abort-if-failed the installed ripper is not the build the handshake record names, or the pair is not the newest — fix that first, the failing step above says which

# --- B. SETTINGS VALIDATION: the cheapest real check in the program --------
# Pure round-trips through the REAL validator, which is the source of truth — a
# spin box's own range is a convenience, not the validation (CLAUDE.md: validate
# every input, visibly and to the log).
#
# Every `set` here is a value we then read back. A silent coercion would show up
# as an `expect` failure rather than as a wrong rip hours later.
#
# THE READ OFFSET IS THE DRIVE'S, not an arbitrary test value — so it is a guard
# and section Q is right not to restore it. `set-drive-offset` keeps the offset
# this machine is already set to, or takes the AccurateRip drive list's, and fails
# if neither is known. On the maintainer's Pioneer BDR-209D that is +667, from
# three independent places: the bundled AccurateRip drive table (whose
# regeneration script REFUSES to write unless the BDR-209D=+667 sentinel still
# passes), `docs/hardware-test-checklist.md` (*"confirmed, two independent
# sources agree"*), and a rip verified byte-identical against the EAC baseline on
# 12 of 14 tracks. Said out loud because the cyanrip fork asked (round 14 lap 3
# §C6) and could not tell a guard from a mistake by reading it.
#
# This used to say "ON ANY OTHER DRIVE, change this to that drive's offset
# before running" — an edit by hand, which a second machine's operator would not
# know to make. The verb makes it unnecessary.

# AND THE VALUE ALONE IS NOT THE SETTING. `read_offset` is inert until
# `override_read_offset` is on: `is_offset_configured()` reads ONLY that flag,
# because cyanrip reads no config file and the number reaches it solely as `-s`,
# emitted solely when the override is set. So a `set read_offset` on its own
# both passes and changes nothing about the rip — the classic shape this file
# already carries three scars from (§5.bj: *a section's distinguishing property
# is asserted at the section, never inherited*), arriving on the one value that
# is pure drive calibration.
#
# What it costs to leave unasserted is not a wrong number, it is a DETOUR: with
# the override off, `_on_rip_requested` calls `_auto_apply_known_offset()`, which
# applies the AccurateRip table's offset and opens an information modal saying
# so. This runner's timer fires inside a modal's nested event loop — that is the
# property that lets a script dismiss dialogs at all — so the batch does not
# deadlock, it keeps walking past a rip that has not started yet. Every accuracy
# section after it would then be about the wrong thing, with the transcript
# green. Two lines are cheaper than that.
log --- B. settings: validated round-trips ---
run-size quick
# THE DRIVE'S OFFSET, NOT A TYPED ONE. This read `set read_offset 667`, which is
# the Pioneer BDR-209D's offset and wrong on every other drive: a second machine
# would have ripped the whole run at the wrong offset, every AccurateRip check
# failing for our reason rather than the disc's. `set-drive-offset` keeps the
# offset this machine is already set to, or takes the AccurateRip drive list's,
# and fails naming the fix if neither is known — so the abort below it holds.
set-drive-offset
expect-drive-offset
expect override_read_offset on
abort-if-failed the read offset for this drive is not known — set the drive up once (Tools, Setup and Updates, Set up drive), then run again
set max_retries 3
expect max_retries 3
# AND PUT IT BACK before anything rips. `max_retries` is cyanrip's `-r`, and
# `-r` is also the ceiling on a secure re-read's whole-track reads: `-Z 2`
# needs three identical reads, so at `-r 3` a single read that disagrees
# leaves the track unverified (the fork's src/cyanrip_main.c:997-1012 at
# faec4a8). Until 2026-09-28 the 3 above rode into every rip until section Q,
# so that day's Full run did every secure re-read in F and N, and their
# automatic re-reads, at `-r 3 -Z 2` with no room for one bad read, instead
# of the shipped `-r 5`. The accuracy sections test what a user gets, so they
# run on the user's default. The round trip above is still the test; this is
# the restore, and `tests/test_rig_scripts.py` checks every rip's ceiling.
set max_retries 5
expect max_retries 5
set output_format flac
expect output_format flac
set force_overread off
expect force_overread off
# THREE SETTINGS NO RIP HERE CAN USE, so each is only round-tripped through the
# validator and goes straight back (TASKS "Permutations the acceptance test
# still does not run"). That proves the value is accepted and stored, and
# nothing about what the setting does: `update_channel` decides only which
# releases Check for updates offers, and no step runs that check (section A's
# `expect-newest-pair` reads the beta channel itself); auto-eject would eject
# the disc every later section needs; and Picard is offered only on the
# unknown-album path, which section E stops the run rather than reach.
set auto_eject_after_rip on
expect auto_eject_after_rip on
set auto_eject_after_rip off
expect auto_eject_after_rip off
set auto_launch_picard on
expect auto_launch_picard on
set auto_launch_picard off
expect auto_launch_picard off
set update_channel beta
expect update_channel beta
set update_channel stable
expect update_channel stable
set ripper_channel beta
expect ripper_channel beta
snapshot settingsafter

# --- C. VALIDATION REFUSALS: proving the guards actually fire ---------------
# The half of validation nothing has ever tested on hardware. `expect-refused`
# asserts the pure validator REJECTS a value **and leaves the setting
# unchanged** — both halves, because a guard that reports a refusal and writes
# the value anyway is worse than no guard: the log says the input was rejected
# while the setting still reaches cyanrip's argv.
#
# These are the numbers that become command-line arguments. A read offset out of
# range rips every subsequent disc wrong with a clean-looking log, which is
# exactly why the range exists and why it is worth one second to prove it holds.

log --- C. validation: every guard must refuse and not write ---
run-size quick
expect-refused read_offset 99999
expect-refused read_offset -99999
expect-refused max_retries 101
expect-refused secure_rerip_matches 11
expect-refused mp3_vbr_quality 10
# A PAIR, not a range: 2 is inside Max retries' own range, and beside the
# default 2 extra matching reads it can never let a secure re-read succeed
# (three identical reads needed, two allowed). The validator refuses the
# pair (since 2026-09-28); this proves it does on the rig, not only in tests.
expect-refused max_retries 2
# And the floor: the guards must not refuse everything. If these were also
# refused, every assertion above would pass for the wrong reason.
expect-drive-offset
expect max_retries 5
snapshot validationdone

# --- D. DIALOGS: everything that can be opened, opened and closed ----------
# Not assertions about text — assertions that opening and closing a dialog does
# not crash, hang, or leave one on screen. `expect-dialog none` at the end is the
# one that catches a dialog that failed to close, which is how a modal comes to
# swallow every later step.
#
# Screenshots for the dense ones (maintainer: "it is a lot"). Every dialog is
# still OPENED — that is the part that can crash.

log --- D. dialogs: open, close, and prove none is left up ---
run-size quick
open drive
screenshot dialogdrive
cancel
open settings
screenshot dialogsettings
cancel
open dependencies
screenshot dialogdependencies
cancel
open about
cancel
open diagnostics
screenshot dialogdiagnostics
cancel
open guide
cancel
open setup
cancel
snapshot dialogsdone

# NO `expect-dialog none` HERE, and the omission is the fix rather than a gap.
#
# **Measured, 2026-08-25 (run 3).** With a disc in the drive, the app identifies
# it at launch and OPENS THE RELEASE PICKER BY ITSELF — before this script
# reaches section D at all. So the picker sits underneath the whole dialog
# section, and an `expect-dialog none` here reported it, correctly, as a
# failure: *"a dialog is open: 'Pick a MusicBrainz release'"*. The assertion was
# true; the expectation was wrong.
#
# The script cannot assert an empty screen before it has answered the picker,
# because having a disc in the drive is a PRECONDITION of this whole run. So the
# assertion moves to just after `pick-release`, where it says something real:
# the picker we answered is gone and nothing else was left behind it.

# --- E. DISC IDENTIFICATION -------------------------------------------------
# The last cheap section. If this fails, nothing after it can mean anything, and
# you have spent five minutes rather than a night finding out.

log --- E. disc: scan and identify ---
run-size quick
rescan
pick-release 1 120
expect-dialog none
expect-tracks 2+
# AND THE GATE THAT COUNTING COULD NOT BE. `expect-tracks` is satisfied by
# PLACEHOLDER rows: a disc MusicBrainz cannot identify still fills the table with
# "Track 01".."Track NN" / "Unknown Artist" (track_table.set_placeholder_tracks),
# so the count passed, the abort below never fired, and every rip for the rest of
# the night would have been evidence about a release nobody chose. This asserts
# the fact instead of a symptom of it: a well-formed MusicBrainz release MBID is
# actually held.
expect-identified
snapshot discidentified

# STOP HERE IF THE DISC WAS NOT IDENTIFIED. The section header above has said
# "if this fails, nothing after it can mean anything" since the file was written,
# and until 2026-08-26 it said so and then carried on for six hours — a comment
# where a check belongs, which is the failure `CLAUDE.md` names by that phrase.
#
# What it costs when the check is absent, measured on the rig the same night: the
# release picker was still open at section F's `rip`, the guard correctly refused
# to press Start behind a modal, and the operator had to answer the picker BY HAND
# to unblock a run whose entire purpose is being unattended. Every rip after that
# point is evidence about a release nobody scripted.
#
# `pick-release` already refuses to pass on a picker that never appeared unless
# tracks are loaded, so a FAIL here is a real one: either the picker did not
# resolve inside its 120 s, or the disc loaded no tracks. Both mean the night is

# Round 16's close condition is fixed at their lap 1 under S-13 and cannot grow.
# Clause 2 is *"`-H` together with de-emphasis produces correct de-emphasised
# audio"*, and this is the only clause no fixture on either side can reach.
#
# WHY IT NEEDS A RIG AND WHY IT NEEDS BOTH FLAGS. Their held item 2 was a filter

# never reached: `-H`, `-H -W` and `-H -E` produced BYTE-IDENTICAL audio, both

# `(deemphasis applied)` and the cue still omitted `FLAGS PRE`, because both read
# the SETTING rather than the audio — so **audio, log and cue were
# self-consistently wrong** and checking any one against another found agreement.
# That is why this step asserts nothing about the log: the log cannot tell you.
#
# THE SEPARATING INPUT IS BOTH FLAGS AT ONCE, which their suite had never used.
# With only one of the two set, selecting and composing are byte-identical, so a
# single run proves nothing whichever way it comes out.
#
# `-E` FORCES DE-EMPHASIS, so this works on ANY disc — it does not need a
# pre-emphasised one, and forcing it is the same graph the TOC flag takes (their
# lap 1 §0 note 1). If the rig disc happens to carry pre-emphasis, plain `-H` is
# the stronger evidence and worth adding; on an ordinary disc `-H -E` against
# `-H -W` is the same code path and not a weaker substitute.
#
# BOUNDED ON PURPOSE. `-l 1` is one track each, so this costs minutes rather than
# a second full rip, and the `cyanrip` verb's own timeout bounds a hang exactly as
# it does in P2. `-s (offset)` is this drive's offset, set in section B; without it
# cyanrip refuses for want of one, which is P2's subject and not this one.
# `-D` takes a RELATIVE naming scheme — confirmed from their source at the pin,
# `cyanrip_main.c:1603`, `folder_scheme`, *"Directory naming scheme"* — so these
# two land beside the run's other output rather than anywhere absolute.
#
# THIS STEP DOES NOT DECIDE THE CLAUSE, AND THAT IS DELIBERATE. Our script
# language has no verb that compares two captures, and inventing one hours before
# an unattended run is how a run gets lost to its own instrumentation. What the
# step does is CAPTURE: the `cyanrip` verb records the exact argv, the exit code
# and the complete output of both runs into the transcript, which the bundle
# carries. cyanrip prints its per-track checksum there, so the verdict is read off
# the returned artifact afterwards, by one comparison:
#
# THIS STEP SETTLES NOTHING, AND EVERY EARLIER VERSION OF THIS COMMENT SAID
# OTHERWISE. Read the next four paragraphs before citing these two runs.
#
# WHAT THIS COMMENT USED TO SAY, AND WHY IT WAS WRONG. It said cyanrip's printed
# per-track checksum "is over the DECODED SAMPLES", and therefore that *"the two

# sentences are false, and the second is the dangerous one.**

# DERIVED FROM THEIR SOURCE AT `ddc1e8c`, not inferred: every checksum cyanrip

# lives. `src/checksums.h:62-90` shows the accumulation itself: EAC CRC32 and
# both AccurateRip sums, straight over the raw bytes. **A checksum taken before
# a filter cannot record what the filter did.**
#
# SO THE TWO ARMS ARE ARITHMETICALLY FORCED TO PRINT THE SAME CHECKSUM, whether
# de-emphasis worked, failed, or was never reached. The old rule therefore
# reported the fork's `b866900` defect as STILL PRESENT on every run that will
# ever be made, including one where the filter composes perfectly -- a false

# be tempted the same way. The old comment argued carefully that `md5sum *.flac`

# and then chose an input that cannot confirm anything either, for the mirror
# reason, while citing the fork as the source of the insight. **The fork had it
# right and we misread why.** Their script prints the container md5s, says in
# its own output that a difference there is "necessary and not sufficient", and
# then DECODES with `ffmpeg -f md5` for the comparison that counts, reporting
# `UNPROBED` rather than a pass when ffmpeg is absent
# (round-16-lap-02-rig-round16.sh:181-212). The decode is the whole mechanism.
# We dropped it because we believed cyanrip had already done it for us.
#
# WHAT THESE TWO RUNS ARE FOR, STATED HONESTLY. They exercise the `-H -E` and
# `-H -W` code paths on real hardware and record the exact argv, the exit code
# and the complete output of each. That is worth having and it is all it is.
